claims.text: Ti-6Al-4V has relatively low baseline surface hardness and moderate wear resistance.
The proposed intervention is laser surface cladding of Ti-6Al-4V with a powder blend containing nitrogen and carbon sources.
The laser cladding is to be performed at approximately 150 J/mm² in an inert atmosphere and followed by controlled cooling.
The powder blend will react in situ with the titanium substrate to form TiN and TiC.
The treatment will produce a near-surface, ultrafine titanium matrix containing a homogeneous dispersion of nanoscale TiN and TiC precipitates.
Rapid melting and fast solidification during laser cladding promote nanocrystallization or substantial grain refinement.
TiN and TiC precipitates inhibit dislocation movement.
TiN and TiC precipitates inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
A TiC-containing laser-cladded surface can be harder than an untreated substrate.
The proposed TiN/TiC laser cladding will increase the surface hardness of Ti-6Al-4V by approximately 50–60% relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
The proposed TiN/TiC laser cladding will reduce the wear rate of Ti-6Al-4V by approximately 40–50% relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
The hardness and wear improvements will hold in ball-on-disk sliding tests from room temperature through 100°C under a constant normal load.
Performance may change when the laser-processing parameters or service temperature exceed the proposed limits.
Process-induced porosity and deviations in laser parameters may cause variability in the uniformity and distribution of TiN and TiC.
